land.text: the Kandyan kingdom, ceded by the Convention of 2 March 1815

successors.note: Cliopatria's British Ceylon row ends in 1814 and has to be checked by sa-06.

capitals.name: Kandy (Senkadagalapura)
capitals.note: The page names Kandy as the capital throughout; coordinates approximate. The city was captured by the Portuguese in 1611 and found evacuated by the British in 1803.

rulers.name: Rajasinha I (of Sitawaka)
rulers.note: The list gives these years; the Sitawaka page has him dead in 1593 or 1594.

correction.text: the central and eastern uplands round Senkadagalapura (Kandy): Kandy, Matale, Nuwara Eliya, Badulla and Monaragala districts

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria's Ceylon runs to 1506 as one island row). Infobox 'Foundation of Senkadagalapura: 1469'; the kingdom was 'in the central and eastern portion of the island', 'initially a client kingdom of the Kingdom of Kotte'. The Kotte page says instead that 'a rebellion led by Senasammata Vikramabahu in 1469 created a new kingdom in the central hill country'. No boundary or area is given: the five districts are my reading of 'central and eastern portion' (about 51 cells of 250 km2).

correction.text: nothing: the kingdom is annexed outright by Sitawaka

keyframe_review.note: Kandy 'was invaded twice during the 1570s and 1580s, first in 1574 and again in 1581', and Rajasinha I 'succeeded in annexing Kandy outright'; infobox 'Conquest by Sitawaka: 1581'. The rulers list shows Kusumasana Devi (1582) and Rajasinha I (1582-1592); the Sitawaka page puts the conquest in 1582. Shown as empty for 1581-1591; the land is Sitawaka's in that dossier.

correction.text: the uplands plus Sabaragamuwa, the Seven Korales (Kurunegala) and the Three and Four Korales hinterland, with the east-coast ports of Trincomalee and Batticaloa

keyframe_review.note: Province table: Uva and Sabaragamuwa '~1592-1815', Sat Korale (Seven Korales, roughly the North Western Province) '~1592-1815', Satara Korale (Four Korales) '~1594-1815'; Uva 'coterminous with the south-western parts of Badulla and Monaragala'; Sabaragamuwa 'coterminous with Ratnapura District'. The ports are in because the Dutch seized them in 1665 (see the ledger). The Kegalle district for the Three and Four Korales and the whole of Kurunegala are my readings. Kalpitiya and Kottiyar are named on the page but are not in the gazetteer and are not drawn.

correction.text: the uplands, the Korales and Kurunegala without Ratnapura: the Dutch seized 'large parts of Sabaragamuwa' and the ports in 1665

keyframe_review.note: 'Seize large parts of Sabaragamuwa in 1665, as well as Kalpitiya, Kottiyar, Batticaloa and Trincomalee'. The French 'seized Trincomalee but were expelled by the Dutch in 1672'. Ratnapura (the table's equivalent of Sabaragamuwa) is removed whole although the page says 'large parts'; the table still lists Sabaragamuwa as Kandyan '~1592-1815', so the removal is shown only until the recaptures of 1675.

correction.text: the uplands, Sabaragamuwa, the Korales and Kurunegala; the ports stay Dutch

keyframe_review.note: 'Kandyan campaigns in 1675 and 1684 recaptured some territory, but by the time of Rajasinha's death in 1687 neither city had returned to Kandyan control'; 'by 1707 Kandyan borders had reopened and both ports were closed'; 'the Kandyans in turn declared war on the Dutch in 1736 and seized some territory'. The page does not say which land the 1675 and 1684 campaigns regained or what the 1736 war added, so nothing but the 1665 shape is drawn.

correction.text: the uplands plus the low country round Matara and Hanwella, annexed in 1761

keyframe_review.note: 'In 1761, however, Kirti Sri Rajasinha launched a major invasion of the low country, annexing Matara and Hanwella'; the war left 'the kingdom on the brink of starvation by 1764'. The Matara circle (25 km) and the Hanwella circle (15 km) are my readings; Hanwella is not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: the uplands, Sabaragamuwa, the Korales and Kurunegala, cut off from the sea

keyframe_review.note: 'By 1765 the Dutch were in a position to force a treaty upon the Kandyans', 'returning not only the border districts but all of Kandy's coastal provinces to the Dutch'; 'henceforth, the kingdom would be effectively cut off from the outside world'. The page lists 21 provinces (12 Disavanis and 9 Ratas) and no area. The infobox map caption reads 'Territorial extent ... (1689-1796)'. The 1766 Treaty of Batticaloa appears only in the province table.

region.text: the central and eastern portion of the island

ledger.note: 1469: Senkadagalapura becomes the seat of a new kingdom. Infobox 'Foundation of Senkadagalapura: 1469'; 'in the central and eastern portion of the island', 'initially a client kingdom of the Kingdom of Kotte'. The Kotte page calls it a rebellion by Senasammata Vikramabahu in 1469. [Repair 2026-10-20: counterpart changed from kingdom-of-kotte to ceylon (kingdom-of-kotte now starts in 1507); ceylon /ledger/16 has the matching loss.]

1581: Sitawaka annexes Kandy. 'Invaded twice during the 1570s and 1580s, first in 1574 and again in 1581'; Rajasinha I 'succeeded in annexing Kandy outright'; infobox 'Conquest by Sitawaka: 1581'. The Sitawaka page says 'in 1582, the new king invaded and conquered the kingdom of Kandy'.

region.text: the Kandyan uplands, recovered from Sitawaka

ledger.note: 1592: Vimaladharmasuriya I recovers Kandy. Infobox 'Ascension of Vimaladharmasuriya I: 1592'; Konnappu Bandara, 'between 1591 and 1594, seized the Kandyan throne'. The Sitawaka page: he 'defeated Rajasinha I in 1593 at Balane and Mawela, effectively securing Kandy's independence from Sitawaka'. 'Portuguese forces briefly occupied Kandy' in 1592.

~1592: Sabaragamuwa and the Seven Korales. Province table: Sabaragamuwa '~1592-1815', 'coterminous with Ratnapura District'; Sat Korale '~1592-1815', 'roughly the North Western Province'. The tilde dates are the page's; the counterpart (Sitawaka's lands, which broke up after 1593) is my reading.

~1594: the Four Korales (Satara Korale '~1594-1815' in the province table). The Sitawaka page says Kandyan forces under Vimaladharmasuriya expelled the Portuguese in 1594 and sacked Sitawaka. The Kegalle district stands in for the Four Korales (my reading).

1611: 'Portuguese forces, acting in the name of the pretender Mayadunne of Uva, captured Kandy'. The page gives no year for their leaving; the occupation is closed at 1612 as a bridging year (page silent) so that the pair is complete.
1612 (bridging): the page gives no year for the Portuguese leaving Kandy after the 1611 capture; the kingdom continues under Senarat (1604-1635).

1665: the Dutch seize the Kandyan ports. The page: the Dutch 'seize large parts of Sabaragamuwa in 1665, as well as Kalpitiya, Kottiyar, Batticaloa and Trincomalee'. Kalpitiya and Kottiyar are not in the gazetteer and are not drawn.
1665: 'large parts of Sabaragamuwa' go to the Dutch (same sentence). The page says 'large parts', the shape removes the whole of Ratnapura District until the recapture.

region.text: Sabaragamuwa, as the province table keeps it Kandyan

ledger.note: 1675: 'Kandyan campaigns in 1675 and 1684 recaptured some territory'. The page names neither the land nor which of the two years took which; Sabaragamuwa is returned in the shape because the province table keeps it Kandyan to 1815 (bridging, page silent).
1761: the low country. 'Kirti Sri Rajasinha launched a major invasion of the low country, annexing Matara and Hanwella.'

region.text: the border districts and all coastal provinces

ledger.note: 1765: the Dutch dictate peace. 'By 1765 the Dutch were in a position to force a treaty upon the Kandyans', 'returning not only the border districts but all of Kandy's coastal provinces to the Dutch'. The infobox and province table give a Treaty of Batticaloa of 1766.

region.text: the whole kingdom, ceded to the British Crown by the Convention

ledger.note: 1815: the British take Kandy. 'Kandy was seized on 14 February, and Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe himself captured on 18 February'; on 2 March 1815 the British and the nobility concluded the Kandyan Convention (infobox '2-18 March 1815'). 'Definitively lost its autonomy following the Uva Rebellion of 1817.'

wars.name: Kandyan-Portuguese wars
wars.outcome: Danture campaign in 1594 (Sitawaka page), defeat at Randeniwela on 2 August 1630, victory at Gannoruwa on 28 March 1638; in May 1638 an alliance with the Dutch. No land changed hands on the pages opened.

wars.name: Dutch seizure of the Kandyan ports
wars.outcome: A 'final break occurred in 1656 in the aftermath of the fall of Colombo'; in 1665 the Dutch seized the ports and large parts of Sabaragamuwa; Kandyan campaigns of 1675 and 1684 won back some land.

wars.name: Kandyan-Dutch war of 1761-1765
wars.outcome: Kandy annexed Matara and Hanwella in 1761; by 1765 'the Dutch were in a position to force a treaty'; all coastal provinces and the border districts went back to the Dutch.

wars.name: First Kandyan War
wars.outcome: 'On 31 January 1803, a British force led by General Hay Macdowall marched to Kandy and found it evacuated'; 'an uneasy truce was in place by 1805'. No land changed hands.

wars.name: British conquest of Kandy
wars.outcome: Kandy seized on 14 February 1815, the king captured on 18 February; the Kandyan Convention on 2 March 1815.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; five districts are drawn for 'central and eastern portion of the island'.
The extent is the province table's modern equivalents ('roughly coterminous'); the page gives neither area nor boundary; the Dutch losses and regains of 1665-1736 name no land.

notes:
No Cliopatria row (Ceylon ends 1506, Portuguese Ceylon 1507-1686, Dutch Ceylon 1687-1795, British Ceylon 1796-1814). Three pages (Kingdom of Kandy, opened twice; Sitawaka and Kotte as mirrors). The Kandy page gives no area and no boundary; every shape is built from the modern districts the province table calls 'roughly coterminous' with Uva, Sabaragamuwa and the Korales.
Disagreements: (1) conquest by Sitawaka 1581 (Kandy infobox and body) against 1582 (Sitawaka page, Kandy rulers list); (2) restoration 1592 (Kandy infobox) against Vimaladharmasuriya's victory over Rajasinha in 1593 (Sitawaka page); (3) 'initially a client kingdom of Kotte' (Kandy) against 'a rebellion ... in 1469' (Kotte): no vassal pair is written; (4) the Treaty of Batticaloa is 1766 in the infobox and table, while the narrative has the Dutch forcing a treaty by 1765; (5) the Kandy page's map caption reads 1689-1796 while the Dutch held the coast from 1665.
Not settled: the extent before 1592 (five districts); what the 1675, 1684 and 1736 campaigns regained; which 'border districts' went back to the Dutch in 1765; where the Seven and Four Korales lay (Kurunegala and Kegalle are my readings); the Portuguese capture of Kandy in 1611 (end year). The overlap with Cliopatria's Portuguese Ceylon shapes (centroid on the west coast, 33,000-61,000 km2) has not been measured.
Counterparts needing a dossier: kingdom-of-kotte and kingdom-of-sitawaka are written in this batch; dutch-ceylon, portuguese-ceylon and british-ceylon belong to sa-06 and should carry the matching gains and losses.
Gazetteer names needed: Hanwella (place), Kalpitiya (place), Kottiyar (place).
